title: Grammar drills
description: Targeted drills for the grammar points that trip up Spanish speakers in English. Each drill has 6-8 questions with explanations.

categories.title: Present perfect vs. past simple
categories.description: Spanish doesn't have a perfect equivalent of the present perfect. The 'have done' form is used for recent events with present relevance, life experiences, and ongoing situations.

rounds.sentence: I _____ to Paris twice in my life.
rounds.explanation: Life experience → present perfect: 'I have been to Paris'.

rounds.sentence: Yesterday I _____ to the cinema with my brother.
rounds.explanation: Specific past time ('yesterday') → past simple: 'I went'.

rounds.sentence: I can't find my keys. Have you _____ them?
rounds.explanation: Past participle after 'have': 'Have you seen them?' (present relevance — the keys are still missing now.)

rounds.sentence: She _____ here since 2019.
rounds.explanation: Ongoing situation from past to present → present perfect: 'She has lived here since 2019.'

rounds.sentence: I _____ a coffee this morning. Do you want one too?
rounds.explanation: Recent event with present relevance → present perfect: 'I have had a coffee' (and the effects are still here — I'm not tired.)

rounds.sentence: When I was a child, I _____ in a small village.
rounds.explanation: Definite finished period in the past ('when I was a child') → past simple: 'I grew up'.

categories.title: Articles (a / the / nothing)
categories.description: English has three options: 'a' (first mention), 'the' (specific), and nothing (plurals/general). Spanish uses 'un/una' and 'el/la' but the rules differ — English drops articles more often than Spanish.

rounds.sentence: I love _____ music. It relaxes me.
rounds.explanation: General statement about music as a category → no article. 'I love music' (not 'the music').

rounds.sentence: Can you pass me _____ salt, please?
rounds.explanation: Specific object we're both looking at → 'the salt'.

rounds.sentence: I met _____ interesting person yesterday.
rounds.explanation: First mention, singular, vowel sound → 'an interesting person'.

rounds.sentence: _____ life is short.
rounds.explanation: General truth → no article. 'Life is short' (life as a concept).

rounds.sentence: I need to go to _____ bank on Fifth Street.
rounds.explanation: Specific bank (named location) → 'the bank on Fifth Street'.

rounds.sentence: She plays _____ piano beautifully.
rounds.explanation: Musical instruments take 'the' in English: 'She plays the piano'.

categories.title: Common prepositions (in / on / at)
categories.description: Prepositions of time and place are different in Spanish. The rule of thumb: in (large/slow), on (surface/specific day), at (point/fast time).

rounds.sentence: I wake up _____ 7 o'clock.
rounds.explanation: Time of day → 'at': 'at 7 o'clock'.

rounds.sentence: We have a meeting _____ Monday.
rounds.explanation: Days → 'on': 'on Monday'.

rounds.sentence: She's on holiday _____ July.
rounds.explanation: Months → 'in': 'in July'.

rounds.sentence: The book is _____ the table.
rounds.explanation: Surface → 'on': 'on the table'.

rounds.sentence: She lives _____ Madrid.
rounds.explanation: Cities / countries → 'in': 'in Madrid'.

rounds.sentence: He's _____ the door. Can you open it?
rounds.explanation: Specific point → 'at': 'at the door'.

categories.title: Conditionals (if sentences)
categories.description: English has 4 conditionals. Spanish speakers often confuse type 2 and type 3, and miss that English has the 'zero conditional' for general truths.

rounds.sentence: If it rains tomorrow, we _____ at home.
rounds.explanation: Type 1 (real future): if + present, will + base. 'If it rains, we will stay'.

rounds.sentence: If I won the lottery, I _____ a house.
rounds.explanation: Type 2 (unreal present): if + past, would + base. 'If I won, I would buy'.

rounds.sentence: If I had studied harder, I _____ the exam.
rounds.explanation: Type 3 (unreal past): if + past perfect, would have + past participle. 'If I had studied, I would have passed'.

rounds.sentence: If you heat ice, it _____.
rounds.explanation: Type 0 (general truth): if + present, present. 'If you heat ice, it melts'.

rounds.sentence: If I _____ you, I would apologize.
rounds.explanation: Type 2: subjunctive 'were' (not 'was') for all subjects in formal English. 'If I were you…'
